lede: Fourteen hundred men rode home from al-Ḥudaybiyah having been turned back from Makkah, with a treaty that looked like surrender. On the road, at night, this surah came down — and called what had just happened a manifest victory. The Prophet ﷺ said it was dearer to him than everything the sun rises upon.

names.name: al-Fatḥ
names.note: From its first ayah. Fatḥ is an opening: of a city, or of a way that had been closed. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal calls the surah by this name when he describes the Prophet ﷺ reciting it on his camel (al-Bukhārī 4281).

revelation.detail: It is Madinan by agreement — meaning after the Hijrah; the place it actually came down was on the road. Al-Qurṭubī relates from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwān that it was sent down between Makkah and Madinah, concerning al-Ḥudaybiyah, from its beginning to its end. That was in Dhū l-Qaʿdah of the sixth year.
revelation.when: On the road back from al-Ḥudaybiyah, at night — Dhū l-Qaʿdah, the sixth year of the Hijrah

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الفَتْحِ وَهِيَ مَدَنِيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
سُورَةُ الْفَتْحِ مَدَنِيَّةٌ بِإِجْمَاعٍ، وَهِيَ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ آيَةً. وَنَزَلَتْ لَيْلًا بَيْنَ مَكَّةَ وَالْمَدِينَةَ فِي شَأْنِ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ

setting: In the sixth year the Prophet ﷺ saw in a dream that he and his Companions entered the Sacred Mosque in safety. He set out for the lesser pilgrimage with some fourteen hundred men, in pilgrim dress, driving the animals for sacrifice, carrying no arms but swords in their sheaths. Quraysh swore that he would never enter, and sent their cavalry to bar the road. He turned aside and halted at al-Ḥudaybiyah, on the edge of the sacred territory.

Envoys went back and forth. He sent ʿUthmān into Makkah; then word came that ʿUthmān had been killed. The Prophet ﷺ sat beneath a tree and the Companions pledged themselves to him, one by one — that they would not flee. That is the Pledge of Good Pleasure, and the surah says of it: “Allah was well pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree.” The report was false. ʿUthmān returned, and Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn ʿAmr to make terms.

The terms were hard to hear. The Muslims would go home without reaching the House, and return the following year for three days. There would be peace for ten years. Any man of Quraysh who came to Muḥammad without his guardian’s leave would be sent back; any Muslim who went over to Quraysh would not. Before the ink was dry, Suhayl’s own son, Abū Jandal, staggered into the camp in chains, and was returned. ʿUmar went to the Prophet ﷺ: “Are we not upon the truth, and they upon falsehood? Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?” He answered: “I am the Messenger of Allah, and I will not disobey Him, and He is my helper.”

They sacrificed where they stood, and turned for Madinah. On the way the surah came. Its first words settled the matter, and events proved them. With the roads open and the fighting stopped, people could meet and listen; al-Zuhrī said that in the two years that followed, as many entered Islam as had done in all the years before, or more. The fourteen hundred of al-Ḥudaybiyah were ten thousand at the conquest of Makkah.

occasions.title: “Dearer to me than all the sun rises upon”
occasions.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was travelling by night with ʿUmar at his side. ʿUmar asked him something and he did not reply — three times — and ʿUmar rode ahead, afraid that Qurʾan would come down about him. Then he heard someone calling him, and came back. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Tonight a surah has been sent down to me that is dearer to me than everything on which the sun rises.” Then he recited: “We have given you a clear victory.”

occasions.title: “And what is there for us?”
occasions.text: Anas said of “We have given you a clear victory”: it is al-Ḥudaybiyah. His Companions said: “Congratulations, and may it bring you joy. But what is there for us?” So Allah sent down: “That He may admit the believing men and the believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow.”
occasions.source: Anas ibn Mālik: al-Bukhārī (4172) and Muslim (1786).

occasions.title: Under the tree
occasions.text: Jābir said: “On the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred, and the Prophet ﷺ said to us: ‘You are the best of the people of the earth.’” And he ﷺ said: “None of those who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire.”
occasions.source: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: al-Bukhārī (4154) and Muslim (1856, 2496).

aim: To recall the divine promise of victory and establishment to His Prophet and to the believers who are true in supporting the religion.

outline.title: The victory, and what it brings
outline.summary: We have given you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you what went before of your sin and what comes after, complete His favour upon you, guide you on a straight path, and help you with a mighty help. It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers, that they might add faith to their faith. He will admit the believing men and women to gardens — and punish the hypocrites and the idolaters, men and women, who think ill of Allah.

outline.title: The pledge
outline.summary: We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news and a warner, that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and honour him and revere him, and glorify Allah morning and evening. Those who pledge allegiance to you are pledging allegiance to Allah: the hand of Allah is over their hands. Whoever breaks it, breaks it against himself; whoever fulfils what he has pledged to Allah, He will give him a great reward.

outline.title: Those who stayed behind
outline.summary: The desert Arabs who stayed behind will say to you, “Our property and our families kept us busy, so ask forgiveness for us.” They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. You thought the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families. When you set out to take spoils they will say, “Let us follow you.” Say: you will be called against a people of great might. There is no blame on the blind, the lame or the sick.

outline.title: Under the tree
outline.summary: Allah was well pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with a victory near at hand, and many spoils that they will take. He has hastened this for you, and held back the hands of people from you.

outline.title: Why there was no battle
outline.summary: Had those who disbelieve fought you, they would have turned their backs. It is He who held back their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah. They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the offering kept from reaching its place. Had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, whom you might have trampled — when the disbelievers put into their hearts the fierce pride of the Age of Ignorance, Allah sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and the believers, and made them hold to the word of mindfulness.

outline.title: The vision will come true
outline.summary: Allah has made true to His Messenger the vision, in all truth: you shall enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security, your heads shaved and your hair cut short, without fear. It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion.

outline.title: Those who are with him
outline.summary: Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah. Those with him are firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure; their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their likeness in the Torah. And their likeness in the Gospel: a seed that puts out its shoot, then strengthens it, so that it grows stout and stands firm on its stem, delighting the sowers.

keyAyah.why: Allah’s own testimony about those fourteen hundred — given not when they won, but when they pledged.

virtues.text: “Tonight a surah has been sent down to me that is dearer to me than everything on which the sun rises.” Then he recited: “We have given you a clear victory.”
virtues.arabic: لَقَدْ أُنْزِلَتْ عَلَيَّ اللَّيْلَةَ سُورَةٌ لَهِيَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا طَلَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ الشَّمْسُ

virtues.text: “I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of the conquest of Makkah, on his she-camel, reciting Sūrat al-Fatḥ in a quavering, resonant voice.”
Al-Barāʾ said: “You count the Victory as the conquest of Makkah — and the conquest of Makkah was a victory. But we count the Victory as the Pledge of Good Pleasure, on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah.”

before: Sūrat Muḥammad: if you help Allah, He will help you — and do not weaken. Al-Fatḥ is the help arriving, by a road no one expected.
after: Al-Fatḥ ends by describing those with the Messenger ﷺ as merciful among themselves. Al-Ḥujurāt sets out what that mercy looks like in daily conduct — towards him, and towards one another.
